thread:
Alex: Heads-up — ran an isolation test for tiny/latency-sensitive requests while background large-batch throughput was high. p50 steady but p95 had long jumps when we did immediate token-reassigns. Thinking hysteresis on steals.
Lina: Can you sketch what you mean by hysteresis here?
Alex: Instead of allowing immediate steal whenever deadline_delta > threshold, require either (a) token age > soft_reserve_ms OR (b) steal_score > hysteresis_threshold, where steal_score increments on observed misses and decays over time.
Chen: That aligns with my concern about oscillation: immediate steals cause batch churn -> more misses -> more steals. A decaying score could dampen that.
Mateo: How do we compute steal_score cheaply? We already track token events. Maybe a sliding counter per-slot + EWMA decay that lives in admission ring buffer.
Lina: Need to consider KV-affinity too. If we steal into a slot with different kv_tags, we pay warmup. Should introduce a penalty factor so steal_score accounts for kv_mismatch_cost.
Alex: Agreed. Proposal: effective_score = base_score - kv_penalty_ms, and require effective_score > hysteresis_threshold. kv_penalty_ms estimated from recent cold-warm latency diffs per model.
Chen: Edge: streaming & pinned sessions should always be excluded. Mark token.kind = {one_shot, streaming, pinned}. Only one_shot participates in hysteresis stealing.
Mateo: API surface: Admit(req, hints) -> TokenHandle. TokenHandle.Meta() returns {kind, kv_tags, created_ts, deadline_hint, slot_id}. TrySteal(new_hints) -> bool with failure reasons exposed for telemetry.
Lina: Telemetry: emit steal_decision{allowed, denied_reason, effective_score, kv_penalty_ms}. Also metric: steal_reblend_rate = steals / tokens_issued per minute.
Alex: For control plane config:
```
{
  "soft_reserve_ms": "6",
  "hysteresis_threshold": "10",
  "steal_score_decay_ms": "200",
  "kv_penalty_weight": "0.7",
  "exclude_kv_mismatch": "false"
}
```
Chen: We should gate this behind an experiment flag and run A/B at tenant level. If steal_reblend_rate correlates with p95 regressions, roll back.
Mateo: One more thought: when hysteresis denies a steal, we can opportunistically mark the incoming request as "fast-forward" to next micro-slice so it gets a shorter wait path (if available) instead of full next-batch. Less intrusive.
Lina: Good idea. That gives graceful degradation without preempting. Implement as hint: prefer_next_slice = true.
Alex: I'll sketch a short RFC with the formulas and a simple state machine. Chen, can you run a microbench measuring kv_cold_penalty per common model profiles?
Chen: Yep. I'll post numbers tomorrow.
op s-bot: experiment/rt-batcher-hysteresis started; canary group = 10% tenants, exp id = 2026-03-21-hys1.
Mateo: Let's meet in 36h with initial bench & telemetry dashboards.
Lina: I'll add the new steal_decision and steal_reblend_rate panels to the runtime dashboard.
Alex: Thanks team — aim for minimal API churn; prefer adding hints rather than reshaping existing structs.
